questions.prompt: GPIS D-19: where is a student's current class kept?
options: In a class_id field on the student
Nowhere as a field: it is derived from the open membership
questions.why: The membership is the one source of truth. The current class is worked out from it.

wrong.0: That is the legacy design, the one GPIS removed.
wrong.1: Two copies drift apart; one of them will be wrong.
wrong.3: A score points to a membership; it does not hold the student's class today.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-21: Ama was in Basic 3A in Term 1 and moved to Basic 3B for Term 2. Her Term 1 card is reprinted in Term 3. Which class and cohort?
options: Basic 3A, ranked among the Term 1 class
questions.why: Her Term 1 scores point to the 3A membership. The card comes from that reference.

wrong.0: That is the legacy bug: today's class on an old card.
wrong.2: A term belongs to exactly one class (D-20).
wrong.3: Nothing is chosen at read time.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-23: a pupil leaves the school in February. What changes?
options: The membership gets an end date, and the student's status becomes withdrawn
The pupil is moved to a class called Left
questions.why: Status and membership are separate facts; a withdrawal changes both.

wrong.1: The membership stays open, and class lists go wrong.
wrong.2: The pupil's history would be lost.
wrong.3: A status is never a class.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-23: where do graduates go?
options: They are deleted after a year
Nowhere: alumni is a status; their memberships and scores stay as they are
questions.why: Nothing moves on graduation. Only the status changes.

wrong.0: Alumni is a status, never a class.
wrong.1: No copy is made; the history stays where it is.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-04: who is on a class list for a term?
options: Students with a membership of that class for that term, and status active
Everyone who ever had a membership of that class
questions.why: Both conditions: the membership places the pupil in the class; the status keeps leavers out.

wrong.0: That lists active pupils of every class.
wrong.1: That includes a withdrawn pupil whose membership was not ended.
wrong.3: That includes pupils who left or moved long ago.

questions.prompt: `type S = "active" | "withdrawn"; const s: S = "Active";` What happens?
options: An error when the program runs
questions.why: "Active" is not one of the two allowed words. The type checker refuses it.

wrong.0: The type check fails before it runs.
wrong.3: Types are removed before running; the check happens at compile time.

questions.prompt: Find the mistake: `type Membership = { …; endedOn?: string }`
options: "Not ended" and "field missing" cannot be told apart; use a required `string | null`
questions.why: null says "known to be open". A missing field could also mean it was never loaded.

wrong.0: `?` is allowed. It is the wrong choice here.
wrong.1: GPIS keeps calendar dates as YYYY-MM-DD text.
wrong.2: A membership that was never loaded would look open.

questions.prompt: GPIS D-20: why may a pupil change class only at a term boundary?
options: So that every term belongs to exactly one class, and a term's scores have one cohort
questions.why: Positions are worked out inside one class for one term. A mid-term move would split the cohort.

wrong.1: That is not the reason given.
wrong.2: Speed has nothing to do with it.
wrong.3: The length of a term is not the reason.
